questions.question: The fifteenth day of the month of June is a Saturday. What will be the last day of the next month which has 31 days?
questions.questionHtml: The fifteenth day of the month of June is a Saturday. What will be the last day of the next month which has 31 days?
questions.solution:
15th June → Saturday

Saturday falls on these dates of June: 15 + 7 = 22; 22 + 7 = 29 and 30th June is Sunday.

1st July falls on Monday. Monday falls on these dates: 1 + 7 = 8; 8 + 7 = 15; 15 + 7 = 22; 22 + 7 = 29

30th July falls on Tuesday and 31st July falls on Wednesday.

questions.question: Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements. Statements: Some boats are ships. All ships are yachts. All yachts are barges. Conclusions: I. Some barges are ships. II. Some barges are boats. III. Some yachts are boats.
questions.questionHtml:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

Statements:

Some boats are ships.

All ships are yachts.

All yachts are barges.

Conclusions:

I. Some barges are ships.

II. Some barges are boats.

III. Some yachts are boats.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions II and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and III follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and III follow

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
options.html: Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
I. Some barges are ships. → Follows (As, All ships are yachts. and All yachts are barges)

II. Some barges are boats. → Follows (As, Some boats are ships, All ships are yachts and All yachts are barges)

III. Some yachts are boats. → Follows (As, Some boats are ships and All ships are yachts)

Hence, 'All conclusions follow' is the correct answer.

questions.question: In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements. Statements: Some roses are yellow. Some yellow are buses. All buses are green. Conclusions: I. All yellow are roses. II. Some buses are yellow. III. All yellow are green.
questions.questionHtml:
In this question, three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statements.

Statements:

Some roses are yellow.

Some yellow are buses.

All buses are green.

Conclusions:

I. All yellow are roses.

II. Some buses are yellow.

III. All yellow are green.
questions.solution:
I. All yellow are roses. → Does not follow (As, Some roses are yellow and Some yellow are buses → Some yellow are roses)

II. Some buses are yellow. → Follows (As, Some yellow are buses)

III. All yellow are green. → Does not follow (As, Some yellow are buses and All buses are green → Some yellow are green)

Hence, 'Only conclusion II follows' is the correct answer.

questions.question: Theoretical foundations of Bharatanatyam have been found in which of these Shastras?
questions.questionHtml: Theoretical foundations of Bharatanatyam have been found in which of these Shastras?
questions.solution: The theoretical foundations of Bharatanatyam can be traced back to the Natya Shastra, an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts written by the sage Bharata. The Natya Shastra covers a wide range of topics related to dance, music, and theater, including the classification of dance forms, the elements of performance, and the roles of the performer and the audience.

questions.solution: The Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian Constitution were borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland, which was adopted in 1937. The Directive Principles of State Policy are a set of guidelines for the government to frame policies and laws that promote the welfare of the people and establish a just and egalitarian society.

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 350 km in 5 hours and covers another 450 km at a speed of 90 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the car?
questions.questionHtml: A car covers a distance of 350 km in 5 hours and covers another 450 km at a speed of 90 km/h. What is the average speed (in km/h) of the car?
questions.solution:
Total distance covered = 350 km + 450 km = 800 km

Total time = 5 hour + 5 hour = 10 hours

Average speed = Total distance/ Total time = 800/10 = 80 km/hr

questions.question: A shopping mart offers four different discounts schemes on the sale of an object as follows: (1) A discount of 30% (2) Two successive discounts of 15% (3) Buy 2, get 1 free (4) Buy 5, get 3 free Which discount scheme offers the maximum discount to a customer?
questions.questionHtml:
A shopping mart offers four different discounts schemes on the sale of an object as follows:

(1) A discount of 30%

(2) Two successive discounts of 15%

(3) Buy 2, get 1 free

(4) Buy 5, get 3 free

Which discount scheme offers the maximum discount to a customer?
questions.solution:
Scheme I. A discount of 30% = 30%

Scheme II. Two successive discounts of 15% = 15 + 15 - (15 × 15)/100 = 30 - 2.25 = 27.75%

Scheme III. Buy 2 get 1 free = (Article get free)/(Total articles) × 100 = 1/(1 + 2 ) × 100 = 33.33%

Scheme IV. Buy 5 get 3 free = (Article get free)/(Total articles) × 100 = 3/(5 + 3) × 100 = 37.5%

questions.question: In a 200-m linear race, if A gives B a start of 25 m, then A wins the race by 10 seconds. Alternatively, if A gives B a start of 45 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does A take to run 200m?
questions.questionHtml: In a 200-m linear race, if A gives B a start of 25 m, then A wins the race by 10 seconds. Alternatively, if A gives B a start of 45 m, the race ends in a dead heat. How long does A take to run 200m?
questions.solution:
Let’s assume speed of A as va and speed of Bas vb

⇒ 175/vb  - 200/va  = 10  ....(1)

if A gives B a start of 45 m, the race ends in a dead heat,

Time taken by B = (200 - 45)/vb = 155/vb

Time taken by A = 200/va

∴ 155/vb = 200/va ⇒ va = 40/31 × vb       ----(2)

Putting (2) in (1) we get, Vb = 2 

Time taken by B to complete 200M race would be 175 / 2 = 87.5 seconds

Thus time taken by A would be = 87.5 - 10 = 77.5 second

questions.question: Ram can copy 60 pages in 15 hours. If Ram and Riya together can copy 180 pages in 30 hours, then in how many hours can Riya copy 20 pages?

The efficiency of Ram and Riya = 180/30 = 6 pages/hr

The efficiency of Riya = 6 - 4 = 2 pages/hr

The time taken by Riya to copy 20 pages will be ⇒ 20/2= 10 hr

questions.question: A can complete a work in 9 days and B in 12 days. If they work together on it for 5 days, then the fraction of the work left is:
questions.questionHtml: A can complete a work in 9 days and B in 12 days. If they work together on it for 5 days, then the fraction of the work left is:
questions.solution:
Total work = L.C.M. of (12, 9) = 36 units

The fraction of the work left is = 1/36

questions.question: An airplane travels five times as fast as a bus. If the bus covers 60 km in 80 minutes, then what distance (in km) will the airplane cover in 25 minutes?

⇒ 135 = (a x 4.5 x 1)/100 ⇒ a = 3000

Additional interest = 150 - 135 = Rs. 15

questions.questionHtml:
Direction: The sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

SO, the correct sequence is CDBA.

questions.question: Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The historians / are a great / asset to the / field of academia.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The historians / are a great / asset to the / field of academia.
questions.solution:
Here, the erroneous part is "The historians."
 

Key Points 

  • The error lies in the part "The historians."
  • The definite article 'the' is used before a noun when one is referring to something specific.
  • In the given sentence, using 'the' before 'historians' would suggest that the speaker is referring to a specific group of historians that have already been mentioned or are known to both speaker and listener.
  • However, when we want to speak generally about all people in a certain group,we should use 'historians' without an article ('the'), similar to how we use 'people' without an article when talking about people in general.

 

Therefore, the​ correct answer is Option 4.

Correct sentence: Historians are a great asset to the field of academia.
